A prolonged disruption beyond September could see Brent retest the ~$120 level seen in April.

We saw in April this year of around about $120. So that's something to keep an eye on. And of course, those talks that were meant to happen this week between Iran and its Gulf counterparts there, they're postponed as well. So we're not sure that deal that we were sort of maybe expecting could happen between Oman and Iran that sort of gone away now certainly in the short term. So yeah, oil nowhere else to go. quote: Last week I was leaning towards staying on hold. And that's because I'm not sure that, you know, hiking interest rates to address what is essentially a supply driven shock courtesy of those high oil prices is the way to go. Having said that, I'm not sure that the fed can really ignore market pricing at the moment and the high expectations for a rate hike to occur this week, so that if I'm forced to make an opinion on it right now, I'm still leaning towards a hold.
